newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia state oil firm to float subsidiary in 97.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia state oil firm to float subsidiary in 97.

text.p: A subsidiary of Indonesia's state-owned oil company Pertamina plans to go public next year, the unit's president director said on Monday.
"We hope we can go public in the first quarter of 1997," Aswad Dipo, president director of PT Elnusa, told reporters.
"The money will be used to expand our business," he said.
"We are still preparing and we hope the listing will be in Jakarta and Surabaya," he said, but gave no other details.
PT Elnusa, wholly owned by Pertamina, supplies gasoline to retail distributors and provides oil and gas services. It is the first subsidiary of Pertamina to seek a listing.
The Jakarta Post said in August that Elnusa booked a pre-tax profit of 37.87 billion rupiah in fiscal 1995/96 (April/March), compared with 28.20 billion rupiah in the previous year.
The company's revenues grew to 370.90 billion rupiah in 1995/96 from 296.83 billion in 1994/95, the paper said.
